quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grips again, then brake again.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until the motorcycle stops completely.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a possible cause of a wobble on your motorcycle?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure
Improper loading
Unsuitable accessories
Uneven road

questions.correctAnswerText: Uneven road
questions.explanation: Most wobbles come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to speed up to get out of a wobble.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, a person age 21 or older with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is considered legally intoxicated.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.06 percent
0.08 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person of legal drinking age with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and unsafe.

questions.question: Which portion of the lane should be avoided?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
No portion of the lane should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No portion of the lane should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best, and no lane position should always be avoided. Choose a lane position that works for the current riding conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: It takes up minimal space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
The group is unlikely to be split up.
The riders will reach their destination faster in a close group than in a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: The riders will reach their destination faster in a close group than in a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a close group is better than riding spread out because the group uses less road space, is easier to see, and is less likely to get separated at traffic lights and during passes.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, it is usually safest to approach the tracks:

options.text: By going straight ahead in your lane.
At a 45-degree angle.
At a 90-degree angle.
At a fast speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: By going straight ahead in your lane.
questions.explanation: It is safest to go straight in your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning to approach the tracks at a right angle can be dangerous because it may push you into another lane.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should tell them to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as they can without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should avoid talking or moving unnecessarily so the rider can focus on the road. Passengers should get on after the engine starts, sit forward without crowding the rider, and hold firmly onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Slow or stop
Left turn
Right turn
Backing up

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow or stop
questions.explanation: Riders can use hand signals instead of or together with turn signals. When the left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing downward, it means the rider plans to slow down or stop.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which should you not do?

options.text: Encourage other friends to talk them out of driving.
Arrange for other transportation.
Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
Slow their pace of drinking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: To prevent someone from driving while intoxicated, arrange other transportation, involve them in other activities to slow their drinking, get other friends to help, and use any excuse to keep them from leaving before they are sober.

questions.question: A motorcyclist can discourage other vehicles from lane sharing by:

options.text: Riding in the left portion of a lane.
Riding in the center portion of a lane.
Giving dirty looks if another driver moves into the lane.
Riding in a zigzag pattern to fill up the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: When a driver might try to squeeze into your lane next to you, ride in the center of the lane to discourage them from doing so.

questions.question: When do you NOT need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When the road is slippery
When there is a lot of traffic
When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
When it is raining

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: You need more following distance when your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your distance if the road is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy and another driver may cut in front of you.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the rear of the group.
Beside the leader.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This puts them near the front of the group where experienced riders behind them can watch and help.

questions.question: What is the best thing to do when it is raining?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side of the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Wet pavement is very slippery when rain first starts. Oil from cars has not washed off yet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars for the safest grip. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: Where should you ride to have the most room to recover from a wind blast?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the middle of your lane gives you the most space to recover if a passing vehicle's wind blast affects your control.

questions.question: How should you stop behind another vehicle?

options.text: Stop far behind, then slowly creep up.
Stay well behind the vehicle.
Make a quick stop right behind the vehicle.
Stay about four car lengths behind the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay well behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when both are stopped. The vehicle could back up, or you may need space to move away from another vehicle coming from behind.

questions.question: Which brakes should you use when making normal stops?

options.text: Only the rear brake.
Only the front brake.
Both the front and rear brakes.
Alternate between the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping. Use both brakes for all stops, even normal ones.

questions.question: Since motorcycles are hard to see at night, what should riders do?

options.text: Reduce their speed when riding at night.
Sound their horn repeatedly when riding at night.
Not ride at night.
Stay directly in front of another vehicle to be seen in their headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed when riding at night.
questions.explanation: Safe night riding includes reducing speed, increasing your following distance, using the headlights of the car ahead to see farther, using your high beam (unless following or meeting another vehicle), and being flexible about your lane position.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When traffic is light.
When traffic is heavy.
When you can see the roadway through vehicles in front of you.
When there is pleasant and clear weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic is heavy.
questions.explanation: A two-second following distance is usually adequate, but increase it when you need more stopping distance. Increase your distance in bad weather, at night, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, and when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Why should you ride on the left side of your lane when preparing to pass on the left?

options.text: The right side could be slippery.
It will give you the best chance of spotting hazards in the next lane.
People don't usually expect to be passed on their left.
It will place you in the rearview mirror of the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will give you the best chance of spotting hazards in the next lane.
questions.explanation: Riding on the left side of your lane improves your view ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic when preparing to pass.

questions.question: How should you load cargo on a motorcycle?

options.text: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Pack lighter items near the front.
Try to not place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Place heavier items in front of the tank bag. Load cargo over or in front of the rear axle. Placing cargo behind the rear axle can affect your control.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see others and be seen.
Keep you away from other drivers' blind spots.
Avoid road hazards.
Block your escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from blind spots and road hazards. Your position should also give you an escape route if a hazard appears. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: When following a car, the best place in the lane to ride is:

options.text: The left portion.
The center portion.
The right portion.
The left or right portions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors. This position makes it more likely they will see you.

questions.question: If you lock the rear tire on a good road surface, you should:

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If you accidentally lock the rear brake on a good road surface, keep it locked until you stop. You can still steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: When riding, the best protection for the rider is:

options.text: Space between your vehicle and other vehicles.
A good leather jacket.
Sturdy boots.
A good understanding of motorcycle laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: Space between your vehicle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keep distance from other vehicles. This is your best protection against crashes. Leave plenty of space so you have time to react if another driver makes a mistake. Wearing proper gear is also important.

questions.question: Fatigue can be increased by:

options.text: Stopping frequently.
Riding in cool weather.
Being comfortable during your ride.
Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in cool weather.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from hard weather like wind and rain to reduce fatigue. Limit riding to six hours per day. Take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because you may feel very tired when they wear off.
